Provider compaction compatibility is implementable and bounded, but the architecture slot goes to a higher-impact approval-trust boundary.
Provider-specific multi-agent capability negotiation is important, but less governance-critical than binding HITL approval to the approving principal.
Excellent session-handoff concurrency mechanism; retained as a high-priority candidate because the selected digital-employee object exposes a sharper evidence-to-memory trust transition.

Ownership-scoped MCP event streaming is a strong lifecycle design; retained behind the selected A2A approval-principal trust boundary.

Managed-instruction continuity across compaction/resume/forks is highly relevant, but the selected digital-employee object is more directly about preventing untrusted evidence from contaminating durable memory.

Malformed catalog-entry isolation improves discovery resilience, but has less security and trust-boundary depth than the selected MCP helper mechanism.
Before-run veto parity restores an important control hook, but is less structurally distinct than the selected MCP helper trust/credential boundary.
Per-agent client injection is useful multi-agent architecture, but does not expose as strong a trust invariant as the selected approval-principal boundary.
An explicit LLM-call budget is valuable runaway-loop control, but narrower than the selected evidence-to-memory trust boundary.

Selected because the maintainer reverted a transport-based A2A HITL guard as both overbroad and insufficient, making the approving principal—not transport metadata—the bounded trust object for human approval.

Per-agent RemoteA2A credential isolation is equally strong on score, but is close to the prior day's credential-boundary topic; retained behind the more structurally distinct principal-vs-transport approval question.

Healthy-runner handoff stability is valuable lifecycle hardening, but the selected digital-employee object presents a more fundamental trust-state transition.
Explicit cross-session delivery failure semantics are strong, but overlap recent asynchronous-delivery work; retained behind the novel approval-principal boundary.

Selected because project MCP helpers can execute code and derive headers, while Folder Trust and stripped inherited credentials establish two separate, testable boundaries: code admission and ambient-secret isolation.

Worker visibility only after claim maps closely to execution-authority semantics and scores highly, but the selected digital-employee object has a broader evidence-integrity consequence without relying on first-party analogy.
Crash reuse and bounded transient-reconnect tolerance are practical recovery mechanisms, but narrower than the selected external-context memory boundary.
Symlink-consistent ignore evaluation is useful filesystem hardening, but has lower governance relevance than the selected MCP helper mechanism.
Releasing old subagent results fixes unbounded memory growth, but is primarily resource management rather than a stronger trust or control boundary.
